beats.headline: A cleric who was expecting him
beats.text: For the record: Crawler Carl reaches the Club Vanquisher door with slugpox, a boil on his stomach, and a ram named Potsy refusing him entry over paperwork. A small man in long red robes pushes the ram aside. I have been waiting for you, he says. Pater Coal, Hobbledehoy, level 101, non-combatant, High Cleric Supreme of Emberus, one of the few mortals in constant contact with the deity. He walks Carl briskly past the mantaur guards toward the healer, with one extra stop at the Emberus shrine that the guards are not to be told about.

beats.headline: Feet washed in the dying sun
beats.text: Sacrament log. In the secret Temple of the Ending Sun, on ground made of fire, Pater Coal suppresses the pox with a spell, kneels, and washes Crawler Carl's feet in boiling water, because Carl is a martyr of Emberus. The other gods cannot eavesdrop on this sacrament. The briefing: no clue to Geyrun's killer but the dog, whose memory the Nothing has spoiled; Hellik still the top suspect; a memorial crystal made by Apito, who lives. Then his eyes go milky white, and the voice names Katia's crossbow and Donut's oak bracelet. Then a toe goes into his mouth.

beats.headline: We all have our roles
beats.text: Crawler Carl tests a suspicion aloud: Zev is worried, because he has dropped off the feed. Back soon enough, the cleric answers without missing a beat, and parts of this conversation still make the feed, so the viewers have context for the quest. Carl asks outright whether he is talking to the AI. We all have our roles, Pater Coal says, and our limitations. Afterwards his pupils fade back to colour, and Emberus grants Carl a floor boon, the Martyr's Path, plus ten percent Strength, for as long as he stays in grace.

beats.headline: The ring that burns
beats.text: Field note from a turkey barn. Crawler Carl ends a deck fight pierced in several places, wrapped in a dead ogre's bear hug and loaded with debuffs, among them one called Bonked. The ring on his finger burns. It looks like his strength ring. It is not. Pater Coal secretly helped him buy it at Club Vanquisher, it is meant to hold certain debuffs at bay, and Carl was warned that it could get overloaded. He cannot take it off.

beats.headline: What if we skip the healer
beats.text: Filed out of order, the way Crawler Carl remembers it. Out of the temple, past a wisp secretary named Yasmine at the portal desk and a mantaur guard admiring himself in a mirror, Pater Coal pulls Carl aside. They must get to the healer quickly, before the guard realises where they have been and bars Carl until tomorrow. Carl, one hand on a boil that has already gone down, asks a different question. What if they do not go to the healer at all?

beats.headline: Interest-free, with an asterisk
beats.text: Transaction record. Beside a satyr jeweler, also of Emberus, Pater Coal prices the work at a million gold. Nobody ever has that much on them; the church is happy to spot it. Ten thousand down, no interest charged to martyrs, and one long-worn piece of jewellery traded in. Carl hands over his first ring. The notice reads interest-free, with an asterisk, for 990,000 gold, and bars him from renouncing his religion while in debt. Carl asks about the asterisk. The jeweler does not understand. Sure, sure, says Pater Coal. Best get this done.

beats.headline: His limitations, remembered
beats.text: Ninth floor. Crawler Carl, turning over how every person and object down here is real, imaginary or somewhere between, comes back to Pater Coal: the high cleric of the Emberus temple at Club Vanquisher, taken over by the AI, who seemed unable to separate the dungeon's story from what was actually being done to the crawlers. We all have our limitations, the cleric had said. Carl's own assessment of that sentence is on file. Terrifying.

beats.headline: Another body, same tenant
beats.text: Growler Gary, the gnoll from the Iron Tangle, is standing in Orren's office and laughing at the liaison. Crawler Carl works it out the way the Emberus temple taught him to: this is not Gary. This is the AI using his body, just as it used Pater Coal's. Orren confirms it and makes the introduction, an avatar for the system AI, and admits he had understood it only took over mobs and NPCs from the current floor.

beats.headline: Find the cleric, says Emberus
beats.text: Outside the temple portal, flat on his back and buried in notifications, Crawler Carl receives another message from Emberus: find Pater Coal, and go talk to somebody. He pushes it away. There are more urgent entries on the same screen. The Emberus ring on his finger is burning, overloaded, and the slugpox it was holding back was never cured.

beats.headline: The same trick, one more time
beats.text: Mid-parade, Grigori takes the microphone and speaks in his own voice, far faster than usual, and it is plain that the AI has taken him over, much as it took Growler Gary and Pater Coal. Crawler Carl's reading of the choice: Grigori is dungeon-born. The man he replaced at the microphone is a former crawler, and the AI does not appear able to do the same with one of those.

relations.note: The church's loan, and the disguised ring
